arxiv-2107-04561.title: Electric Field Decay Without Pair Production: Lattice, Bosonization and Novel Worldline Instantons
arxiv-2107-04561.creator: Xu-Yao Hu, Matthew Kleban, and Cedric Yu
arxiv-2107-04561.description: Abstract Electric fields can spontaneously decay via the Schwinger effect, the nucleation of a charged particle-anti particle pair separated by a critical distance d d . What happens if the available distance is smaller than d d ? Previous work on this question has produced contradictory results.

arxiv-2108-01051.title: Evolution of proto-neutron stars to pulsars, magnetars and central compact objects
arxiv-2108-01051.creator: İrem Bakır, Kazım Yavuz Ekşi
arxiv-2108-01051.description: Abstract Some of the young neutron stars, the magnetars, have ultra-strong magnetic fields. The models invoked for the origin of magnetar fields require very specific conditions with extreme parameters, which are incompatible with the inference that the birth rate of magnetars is comparable to the rate of core-collapse supernovae.

arxiv-2303-09296.title: Disconnected Common Graphs via Supersaturation
arxiv-2303-09296.creator: Jae-baek Lee, Jonathan A. Noel
arxiv-2303-09296.description: Abstract A graph H H is said to be common if the number of monochromatic labelled copies of H H in a 2 2 -colouring of the edges of a large complete graph is asymptotically minimized by a random colouring. It is well known that the disjoint union of two common graphs may be uncommon; e.g.

arxiv-2503-13059.title: Non-existence of symmetric biderivations on finite-dimensional perfect Lie algebras
arxiv-2503-13059.creator: Ignacio Bajo, Saïd Benayadi, Hassan Oubba
arxiv-2503-13059.description: Abstract We show that there are no symmetric non-zero biderivations on perfect Lie algebras of finite dimension over a field of characteristic zero. We show that this is equivalent to show that every symmetric biderivation on a finite-dimensional perfect Lie algebra over such a field with values in a finite-dimensional module vanishes identically.

arxiv-2503-24307.title: A Systematic Evaluation of LLM Strategies for Mental Health Text Analysis: Fine-tuning vs. Prompt Engineering vs. RAG
arxiv-2503-24307.creator: Arshia Kermani, Veronica Perez-Rosas, Vangelis Metsis
arxiv-2503-24307.description: Abstract This study presents a systematic comparison of three approaches for the analysis of mental health text using large language models (LLMs): prompt engineering, retrieval augmented generation (RAG), and fine-tuning. Using LLaMA 3, we evaluate these approaches on emotion classification and mental health condition detection tasks across two datasets.

arxiv-2508-14268.title: Comparing Model-agnostic Feature Selection Methods through Relative Efficiency
arxiv-2508-14268.creator: Chenghui Zheng, Garvesh Raskutti
arxiv-2508-14268.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Chenghui Zheng, Garvesh Raskutti. Feature selection and importance estimation in a model-agnostic setting is an ongoing challenge of significant interest. Wrapper methods are commonly used because they are typically model-agnostic, even though they are computationally intensive. In this paper, we focus on feature selection methods related to the Generalized Covariance Measure (GCM) and Leave-One-Covariate-Out (LOCO) estimation, and provide a comparison based on relative efficiency.

arxiv-2510-22770.title: Feedback approximate controllability of blowup points for the heat equation with anti-interference blowup profile
arxiv-2510-22770.creator: Ping Lin, Hatem Zaag
arxiv-2510-22770.description: Abstract Abstract. This paper is concerned with a feedback approximate controllability problem of blowup points for the heat equation. We show that the system is approximately controllable for blowup points with feedback controls and the feedback operator is bounded at any time before blowup.

pmc-10626402.title: Do we correctly calculate doses of cardioplegia during aortic valve replacement procedures? A preliminary report
pmc-10626402.creator: Aleksandra Sucharska, Agnieszka Adamowska, Zuzanna Karbowska, Lavanya Mohan Kumar, Jakub Pudełko, Łukasz Szarpak, Marek Jemielity, Bartłomiej Perek
pmc-10626402.description: IntroductionIntraoperative myocardial protection during aortic valve replacement (AVR) for aortic stenosis (AS) is of paramount importance for outcomes. The dose of cardioplegia is usually calculated with reference to body mass.AimTo assess whether such a strategy should be applied to all AS patients undergoing AVR.

pmc-10692957.title: Protocol for generating embedding-free brain organoids enriched with oligodendrocytes
pmc-10692957.creator: Bahaa Al-mhanawi, Marta Boira Marti, Sean D Morrison, Pallavi Gupta, Maath Alani, Peter G Noakes, Ernst J Wolvetang, Mohammed R Shaker
pmc-10692957.description: SummaryIn response to the scarcity of advanced in vitro models dedicated to human CNS white matter research, we present a protocol to generate neuroectoderm-derived embedding-free human brain organoids enriched with oligodendrocytes. We describe steps for neuroectoderm differentiation, development of neural spheroids, and their transferal to Matrigel. We then detail procedures for the development, maturation, and application of oligodendrocyte-enriched brain organoids.

pmc-11406999.title: Atlas of telomeric repeat diversity in Arabidopsis thaliana
pmc-11406999.creator: Yueqi Tao, Wenfei Xian, Zhigui Bao, Fernando A Rabanal, Andrea Movilli, Christa Lanz, Gautam Shirsekar, Detlef Weigel
pmc-11406999.description: BackgroundTelomeric repeat arrays at the ends of chromosomes are highly dynamic in composition, but their repetitive nature and technological limitations have made it difficult to assess their true variation in genome diversity surveys.ResultsWe have comprehensively characterized the sequence variation immediately adjacent to the canonical telomeric repeat arrays at the very ends of chromosomes in 74 genetically diverse Arabidopsis thaliana accessions.

pmc-11496547.title: Radiation dermatitis in the hairless mouse model mimics human radiation dermatitis
pmc-11496547.creator: Jessica Lawrence, Davis Seelig, Kimberly Demos-Davies, Clara Ferreira, Yanan Ren, Li Wang, Sk. Kayum Alam, Rendong Yang, Alonso Guedes, Angela Craig, Luke H. Hoeppner
pmc-11496547.description: Over half of all people diagnosed with cancer receive radiation therapy. Moderate to severe radiation dermatitis occurs in most human radiation patients, causing pain, aesthetic distress, and a negative impact on tumor control. No effective prevention or treatment for radiation dermatitis exists.

pmc-11532379.title: Early warning model to detect anastomotic leakage following colon surgery: a clinical observational study
pmc-11532379.creator: Pooya Rajabaleyan, Ravish Jootun, Sören Möller, Ulrik Deding, Mark Bremholm Ellebæk, Issam al-Najami, Ian Lindsey
pmc-11532379.description: PurposeWe aimed to develop a predictive tool for anastomotic leakage (AL) following colon cancer surgery by combining a clinical early warning score (EWS) with the C-reactive protein (CRP) level.MethodsThe records of 1,855 patients who underwent colon cancer surgery at the Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust between January 2013 and December 2018, with or without AL, were retrospectively reviewed.

pmc-11639182.title: How pairs of insertion mutations impact protein structure: an exhaustive computational study
pmc-11639182.creator: Changrui Li, Yang Zheng, Filip Jagodzinski
pmc-11639182.description: SummaryUnderstanding how amino acid insertion mutations affect protein structure can inform pharmaceutical efforts targeting diseases that are caused by protein mutants. In silico simulation of mutations complements experiments performed on physical proteins which are time and cost prohibitive. We have computationally generated the exhaustive sets of two amino acid insertion mutations for five protein structures in the Protein Data Bank.

pmc-12533582.title: A choline-sensing regulator coordinates metabolic adaptation and pathogenesis in Pseudomonas aeruginosa pulmonary infections
pmc-12533582.creator: Yingjie Song, Xiyu Wu, Bo Song, Ziqi Zhu, Derong Dai, Qinqin Ma, Rui Bao
pmc-12533582.description: Pseudomonas aeruginosa exploits host-derived phosphatidylcholine (PC) to establish persistent lung infections, yet the mechanistic link between metabolic adaptation and pathogenesis remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate that choline (Cho)–induced regulator (CodR), a GcvA-type transcriptional regulator, serves as a master regulator integrating virulence, antibiotic resistance, and PC catabolism during pulmonary infection.

pmc-12552756.title: Stakeholder Perspectives on Retention Strategies for Rehabilitation Professionals: A Qualitative Study
pmc-12552756.creator: Susanne Mak, Matthew Hunt, Saleem Razack, Kelly Root, Aliki Thomas
pmc-12552756.description: There is a scarcity of health human resources worldwide. In occupational therapy (OT), physical therapy (PT), and speech-language pathology (S-LP), attrition and retention issues amplify this situation and contribute to the precarity of health systems. Therefore, we aimed to investigate retention strategies for rehabilitation professionals in Quebec.

pmc-12562283.title: Cellulose-Derived Gels for Topical Delivery: HPMC as a Functional Matrix for Porphyrinic Photosensitizers
pmc-12562283.creator: Emma Adriana Ozon, Andreea Mihaela Burloiu, Adina Magdalena Musuc, Gina Manda, Valentina Anuta, Cristina Elena Dinu-Pîrvu, Dumitru Lupuliasa, Ionela Victoria Neagoe, Mihai Anastasescu, Radu Petre Socoteanu, Irina Atkinson, Raul-Augustin Mitran, Daniela C Culita, Rica Boscencu, Željka Vanić, Paula M
pmc-12562283.description: Hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC) is a biocompatible polymer widely used in topical formulations due to its suitable rheological behavior, film-forming capacity, and good compatibility with different active pharmaceutical ingredients. The present study demonstrates the potential of HPMC-based gels for dermal delivery of porphyrinic photosensitizers, aiming to enhance the efficiency of photodynamic therapy (PDT) in potential skin cancer applications.

pmc-12565637.title: Advantages and Disadvantages of the Arthroscopic Procedure in Acromioclavicular Separation
pmc-12565637.creator: Mihai Tudor Gavrilă, Vlad Cristea, Stefan Cristea, Silvia Giovannini, Yuji Uchio
pmc-12565637.description: Arthroscopic treatment of acromioclavicular (AC) joint separations has evolved significantly over the past two decades. Modern anatomical repair methods frequently rely on suspensory fixation devices to reconstruct the coracoclavicular ligaments and, in some cases, to stabilize the AC joint itself.

pmc-12566904.title: Fractional Anisotropy Alterations in Key White Matter Pathways Associated with Cognitive Performance Assessed by MoCA
pmc-12566904.creator: Nauris Zdanovskis, Kalvis Kaļva, Ardis Platkājis, Andrejs Kostiks, Kristīne Šneidere, Guntis Karelis, Ainārs Stepens, Francesco Di Lorenzo
pmc-12566904.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Objectives: This study investigated fractional anisotropy (FA) differences within key white matter tracts across patient groups stratified by Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) scores, aiming to evaluate FA’s potential as a biomarker for cognitive impairment. Methods: Seventy participants (aged 57–96 years) were categorized into high (HP, MoCA ≥ 26), moderate (MP, MoCA 18–25), and low (LP, MoCA < 18) cognitive performance groups. Diffusion Tensor Imaging (DTI) was used to obtain FA values in corticospinal tracts, superior longitudinal fasciculus, inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus, and cingulum.

pmc-12579360.title: In‐Depth Assessment of Cytologic Features in 106 Cervical Papanicolaou Tests of Transgender Male Patients on Testosterone: An Institutional Experience
pmc-12579360.creator: Juanita E. Ferreira, Nikki Chiang, Xin Jing, Brian Smola, Richard L. Cantley, Judy C. Pang, Madelyn Lew
pmc-12579360.description: BackgroundThere is a decreased cervical cancer screening rate among female to male transgender (FTMTG) patients. Data on the distinct cytologic features present in cervical cytology (CC) of those on testosterone therapy is limited.MethodsAn 2017–2023 electronic database search identified CC specimens from a cohort of FTMTG patients on testosterone therapy (TT).

pmc-12845113.title: The Dual Role of Nrf2 Signaling in Virus Infections: Antiviral Guardian or Proviral Accomplice?
pmc-12845113.creator: Bikash R. Sahoo, Kush K. Pandey, Asit K. Pattnaik
pmc-12845113.description: The transcription factor nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) plays a critical role in regulating cellular defense against oxidative stress and maintaining redox homeostasis. In the context of viral infections, Nrf2 signaling emerges as a double-edged sword. On one hand, it activates a broad spectrum of antioxidant and cytoprotective genes, contributing to host defense and antiviral immunity.

pmc-12908412.title: Astrocytes in the glioblastoma tumor microenvironment
pmc-12908412.creator: Camilo Faust Akl, Brian M Andersen, Francisco J Quintana
pmc-12908412.description: ance of GBM-astrocyte interactions, which exist at the invasive borders of GBM.1 Bidirectional functional interactions between astrocytes and other cells in the central nervous system (CNS) control the local immune response, as well as astrocyte heterogeneity.2,3 In recent studies, we identified astrocyte subsets that limit the immune response to GBM through their interactions with either T cells or tumor cells.

pmc-13153178.title: Intra-operative application of ultra-high frequency ultrasound facilitates differentiation of bowel wall characteristics between ganglionic and aganglionic segments during transanal endorectal pull-through for Hirschsprung disease
pmc-13153178.creator: Christina Granéli, Maria Evertsson, Tobias Erlöv, Tebin Hawez, Kristine Hagelsteen, Louise Tofft, Tomas Jansson, Magnus Cinthio, Pernilla Stenström
pmc-13153178.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThe hypothesis was that ultra-high-frequency (UHF) ultrasound can distinguish ganglionic from aganglionic bowel during surgery for Hirschsprung disease. The aim was to assess UHF ultrasound for differentiating ganglionosis from aganglionosis in children undergoing rectosigmoid Hirschsprung disease surgery.MethodsThe child’s intestine was examined intra-operatively using the Vevo MD (Fujifilm VisualSonics, Toronto, ON, Canada) system equipped with the UHF70 transducer; 50 MHz in center frequency. Collected images were analyzed and results presented as median.ResultsTwenty-one patients were examined intra-operatively with UHF ultrasound.

pmc-13281635.title: The influence of physical activity on circadian syndrome: a nationwide prospective study based on the CHARLS cohort
pmc-13281635.creator: Datong Li, Mian Sun, Wanyu Jiang
pmc-13281635.description: BackgroundA major public health concern is the increasing incidence of circadian syndrome (CircS), especially in older people. While physical activity (PA) is recognized for its metabolic benefits, its longitudinal association with CircS, especially in the Chinese context, remains to be fully elucidated. This research sought to investigate this relationship using a national longitudinal cohort.

pmc-13296334.title: Presbycusis Across the Lifespan: Genetic, Molecular, and Multi-Omics Contributions
pmc-13296334.creator: Anna Morgan, Paolo Gasparini, Giorgia Girotto
pmc-13296334.description: Presbycusis, or age-related hearing loss (ARHL), is a multifactorial disorder characterized by a gradual, bilateral sensorineural decline in hearing sensitivity, predominantly affecting high-frequency sounds. It is one of the most common chronic conditions in the aging population and represents a major public health concern due to its high prevalence and progressive nature.

pmc-13347065.title: Genetic and molecular signatures highlight diverse pathways linking obesity to type 2 diabetes
pmc-13347065.creator: Pascal M. Mutie, Tijana Stojanovic, Valeria Lo Faro, Torgny Karlsson, Åsa Johansson
pmc-13347065.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Obesity is a major risk factor for type 2 diabetes, a disease affecting approximately 10% of the global population. Obesity is a heterogeneous condition, with different components exerting distinct, and sometimes opposing, effects on type 2 diabetes risk. Here, we aim to identify molecular mechanisms through which distinct components of obesity influence risk for type 2 diabetes by integrating multi-omics data.

pmc-13358744.title: Dermatoses in Pregnancy: A Hospital-Based Cross-Sectional Study From Eastern India
pmc-13358744.creator: Doyir Bagra, Debabrata Ghosh, Sudipta Biswas, Koushik Biswas, Kaushik Shome, Joly Seth

pmc-13386259.title: Remission duration according to dietary adherence in paediatric mild to moderate Crohn’s disease treated with CDED + PEN
pmc-13386259.creator: Anna Wiernicka, Izabela Jałocha, Małgorzata Garwolińska
pmc-13386259.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionThe Crohn’s Disease Exclusion Diet (CDED) combined with partial enteral nutrition (PEN) is a dietary therapy developed to induce and maintain remission in patients with Crohn’s disease.AimThe aim of study was to evaluate the duration of clinical remission in paediatric patients with mild to moderate Crohn’s disease undergoing a Crohn’s Disease Exclusion Diet (CDED) combined with partial enteral nutrition (PEN), stratified by degree of dietary adherence.Material and methodsA retrospective, single-centre observational study was conducted with the participation of paediatric patients who underwent

pmc-13473500.title: Acute effects of an individually timed lower-limb post-activation performance enhancement protocol on 50 m front crawl performance and race kinematics in national-level swimmers
pmc-13473500.creator: Arkadiusz Stanula, Marek Strzała, Wojciech Sadowski, Wojciech Rejdych, Katja Weiss, Jakub Karpiński, Robert Wilk, Thomas Rosemann, Beat Knechtle
pmc-13473500.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Post-activation performance enhancement (PAPE) has been proposed as an acute strategy to improve explosive performance, yet its effects on sprint-swimming performance remain unclear, particularly when individualized recovery timing is considered. This study examined the acute effects of a lower-limb PAPE protocol, applied using an individually determined recovery time (IRT), on 50 m front crawl performance and selected start-, race-, and turn-related kinematic variables in national-level male swimmers.

pmc-13538326.title: A rare case of multisystem autoimmune disease presenting with retinopathy and alopecia post COVID-19 vaccination
pmc-13538326.creator: Srinivasan Sanjay, Samanthila Waduthantri, Manju Chandran, Soon-Phaik Chee
pmc-13538326.description: PurposeTo report a case of autoimmune retinopathy (AIR) with multiple systemic involvementResultsA 45-year-old Asian Indian male presented with progressive blurring of vision in the right eye for five years. Initial best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) was 20/80 in RE and 20/25 in LE. Clinical evaluation was normal except for a few pigmentary alterations in the periphery.
